decisions.what: Used a tsup programmatic build script to generate an opaque pre-bundle generation and inject it via define before bundling.
decisions.why: The generation must be defined before the bundler runs and then written to the sidecar after index.js exists; the script is the only place that can both inject and finalize.

decisions.what: Captured the loaded generation at module evaluation in plugin-bundle-manifest.ts and imported it from index.ts.
decisions.why: Keeps the generation concern in the manifest module and wires module-evaluation capture without scattering logic in index.ts.

decisions.what: Made files.index diagnostic-only and used generation equality as the staleness authority.
decisions.why: Satisfies AC5: a deployment that preserves index.js mtime but changes the manifest generation still reports stale.

decisions.what: Centralized plugin root / dist path resolution in plugin-bundle-manifest.ts via getPluginRoot() and getPluginBundleDistDir().
decisions.why: Both index.ts and plugin-runtime-info.ts need the plugin root; computing it locally with ../.. from one-level-deep index.ts or from a bundled dist/chunk was producing repo-root instead of plugin-root. A single source-of-truth helper anchored to plugin-bundle-manifest.ts's location (always one level under plugin root) removes the per-callsite arithmetic.

decisions.what: Added optional moduleUrl parameter to the helpers so tests can simulate source and bundled module paths.
decisions.why: Tests run from source and cannot easily observe production bundling; the parameter lets regression tests assert the resolution for src/index.ts, dist/index.js, and dist/chunk-*.js without relying on the actual build.

decisions.what: Removed local dirname/fileURLToPath imports from index.ts and plugin-runtime-info.ts where only the plugin root was needed.
decisions.why: Eliminates the duplicated, fragile path math and keeps the resolution logic in one place.

decisions.what: Made the plugin manifest part of the deploy-time stale check so missing manifests trigger a rebuild before the guard fires.
decisions.why: The stale check already enforces required dist outputs; treating the manifest as a required output is the simplest structural guard and avoids a redundant failure path in normal builds.

decisions.what: Skipped the manifest file existence guard in --dry-run mode.
decisions.why: Dry-run is a preview and may legitimately show a stale dist that would be rebuilt; failing on a missing manifest would break the existing dry-run preview behavior.

decisions.what: Used sha256sum with shasum fallback for index validation.
decisions.why: Keeps the script portable across Linux (sha256sum) and macOS (shasum).

decisions.what: Used jq to extract the expected hash from the manifest.
decisions.why: jq is already a documented dependency for deploy-local --fix config patching, so reusing it avoids adding another tool.

subagent_reports.topic: Design leverage opportunity scout for stale plugin bundle detection

sources.label: Approved agreement
sources.summary: Defines generation equality, typed stale/unknown states, health output, one system banner, deployment refusal, mtime diagnostics only, and no hot reload.

sources.label: Existing plugin runtime diagnostics
sources.summary: PluginRuntimeInfo already centralizes runtime provenance; current freshness authority is mtime-based and getPluginRuntimeInfo reads diagnostics on demand.

sources.label: Existing status health seam
sources.summary: adv_status already returns plugin_runtime in the health-oriented output assembly.

sources.label: Existing worker manifest pattern
sources.summary: Worker manifest documents content-derived generation and temp-file plus same-directory rename, while its reader collapses invalid states to null.

sources.label: Single system-block assembler
sources.summary: System diagnostics are composed through one pure ordered formatter; existing session-health state is narrowly typed.

sources.label: Current deployment sync
sources.summary: Deployment currently performs one whole-plugin rsync after source-dist freshness checks.

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: CAUTION. Strongest leverage is extending existing plugin-runtime-info, status health output, and single system-block assembler instead of creating parallel diagnostics. Design should preserve a distinct loaded embedded generation, return discriminated unknown reasons, keep stale banner state independent from session-health hazards, and make manifest publication the explicit last deployment step. Reuse worker manifest semantics as a pattern, not its worker-specific API.

validation.notes: Agreement is coherent, but no draft design artifact was available to confirm these seams and deployment ordering are explicitly handled.

tradeoffs: Adding typed identity fields to PluginRuntimeInfo keeps one diagnostics seam but expands an existing public output contract.
Discriminated unknown reasons improve diagnosis but require a bounded enum and parser test matrix.
Publishing the manifest last strengthens commit-marker semantics but makes deployment flow more explicit than one whole-tree rsync.
Keeping plugin and worker manifests separate duplicates small mechanics but avoids a premature cross-domain abstraction.

alternatives_considered.option: Create a separate plugin freshness subsystem and status probe
alternatives_considered.rationale: Duplicates existing PluginRuntimeInfo and status health seams.
Would couple plugin freshness to session-history hazard state and conflicts with DONT3.
Current module is worker-specific; one additional consumer does not yet justify a generic framework.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep whole-tree rsync without explicit manifest-last publication
alternatives_considered.rationale: Simpler deployment, but design must first prove it preserves sidecar commit-marker semantics.

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Adopt candidates 1-3 now, design around candidate 5, and explicitly decide candidate 4 before validator review.

subagent_reports.recommendation: Carry four design decisions into draft: extend PluginRuntimeInfo; model unknown with bounded reason codes; add an independent stale section to the single system block; keep plugin manifest implementation local. Surface deployment manifest-last publication for explicit design resolution.
follow_ups: Packet omitted IN_SCOPE, OUT_OF_SCOPE, DONE_WHEN, STOP_WHEN, and VERIFICATION anchors; scout followed TASK_SCOPE and embedded agreement without inferring missing boundaries.
Episode recall returned no relevant prior decision; prior_consideration remains unknown and must be supplied by orchestrator conflict scan.
Candidate details are returned in the user-facing response; no files were edited.

subagent_reports.topic: Independent design validation for stale plugin bundle detection

sources.label: Approved agreement
sources.summary: Requires immutable generation equality, typed stale/restart recovery, safe bounded unknown states, mtime-independent detection, health projection, exactly one stale section, missing-manifest deploy refusal, no hot reload, and no session-health overwrite.

sources.label: Proposed design
sources.summary: Proposes one embedded plugin generation, final index.js SHA-256, atomic plugin-specific manifest, additive PluginRuntimeInfo diagnostics, independent system-block section, and manifest-last deployment.

sources.label: Runtime provenance spec law
sources.summary: Requires existing dist/source/process freshness fields and structured recovery hint in adv_status health, graceful null degradation, and no in-surface rebuild/restart orchestration.

sources.label: Single system-block spec law
sources.summary: Requires at most one ADV-controlled output.system entry per transform and assembly of all warning/context sections into output.system[0].

sources.label: Existing plugin runtime seam
sources.summary: PluginRuntimeInfo already owns runtime provenance; existing source_dist_freshness has a separate four-value contract and recovery_hint is structured.

sources.label: Existing health projection
sources.summary: adv_status detailed output already exposes plugin_runtime through the health-capable assembly path.

sources.label: Existing single system-block assembler
sources.summary: One pure formatter appends into output.system[0]; session health is a narrow independent state field.

sources.label: Current transform call site
sources.summary: Each system transform currently calls applyAdvSystemBlock synchronously from an async hook, but no deployed plugin manifest refresh input exists yet.

sources.label: Existing worker manifest pattern
sources.summary: Established local pattern hashes bundle output and publishes a same-directory temp file by rename after payload output.

sources.label: Current build pipeline
sources.summary: Full build invokes main tsup, then build:worker, then build:identity; build:worker invokes tsup separately, making plugin-only generation scoping necessary.

sources.label: Current deployment pipeline
sources.summary: Freshness guard currently checks required outputs and mtimes; plugin manifest is not yet required.

sources.label: Current deployment sync
sources.summary: Current deployment uses one rsync of the plugin tree, so manifest-last publication requires explicit exclusion/staging rather than relying on present ordering.

sources.label: Official tsup configuration docs
sources.summary: Documents esbuildOptions/define for compile-time replacement and async onSuccess hooks; these provide supported primitives for embedding a build value and post-JavaScript-output finalization.

sources.label: Official tsup source example
sources.summary: Shows tsup forwarding options.define into esbuild's define map, supporting build-time constant injection.

sources.label: Node.js crypto API
sources.summary: Documents createHash and SHA-256 update/digest usage for output hashing.

sources.label: Node.js filesystem API
sources.summary: Documents promise-based rename used by the existing manifest publication pattern.

sources.label: POSIX rename specification
sources.summary: Specifies atomic rename replacement semantics, supporting same-directory temp-file publication on the target POSIX environment.

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: CAUTION. Core architecture is correct and simpler than timestamp authority or hot reload: capture one immutable build generation in loaded code, compare it with a sidecar generation, retain SHA-256 and built_at as provenance, degrade invalid reads to typed unknown, and surface stale state through existing runtime-info/status/system-block seams (agreement; proposed design; Node crypto docs; POSIX rename spec). Two design details need explicit closure before implementation: (1) AC7 requires the deployed manifest to be re-read and compared on every system transform, or through an equivalently guaranteed refresh path, because current transform input has no plugin-freshness source; init-only capture would miss a later deploy (current transform call site). Keep IO outside the pure assembler and pass a typed snapshot into it. (2) Define generation creation as one pre-bundle, non-content-derived opaque value shared by compile-time injection and manifest finalization; using the final index hash as the embedded generation would create self-reference. Hash final index.js separately as agreed. Preserve existing source_dist_freshness and recovery_hint fields additively because rq-runtimeProvenance01 still requires them. Manifest-last deployment is sound as a visibility marker only if the first rsync excludes the manifest and final publication validates/copies it separately; current one-pass rsync does not provide that ordering.

validation.notes: No contract, security, or release blocker found. Design satisfies agreement direction and applicable spec laws, but next-transform refresh semantics, non-self-referential generation creation, additive runtime field naming, and concrete manifest-last deploy mechanics must be explicit in planning/implementation criteria.

tradeoffs: Reading and validating a small manifest on every system transform gives exact AC7 behavior but adds bounded filesystem IO to each transform; caching must not weaken next-transform detection.
A random or otherwise opaque per-build generation distinguishes identical repeated builds, while the separate SHA-256 preserves content provenance; this uses two identity values instead of one.
Keeping a plugin-specific manifest duplicates small worker-manifest mechanics but avoids a premature generic bundle-manifest framework.
Manifest-last rsync staging improves visibility semantics but does not make the full payload copy transactional; a session starting mid-copy can still encounter deployment-transient behavior.
Additive PluginRuntimeInfo fields preserve spec compatibility but expand the health output contract and test matrix.

alternatives_considered.option: Opaque pre-bundle generation embedded through tsup define, plus separate final index.js SHA-256
alternatives_considered.rationale: Supported by tsup define and Node crypto APIs; avoids self-referential hashing while satisfying loaded-versus-deployed equality and provenance requirements.

alternatives_considered.option: Use final index.js SHA-256 as the embedded generation
alternatives_considered.rationale: Embedding the value changes the file being hashed, creating a circular identity problem unless a more complex canonicalization scheme is introduced.

alternatives_considered.option: Retain process-start/mtime freshness as stale authority
alternatives_considered.rationale: Contradicts approved C1/DONT2 and cannot satisfy the mtime-preserved deployment criterion.
Contradicts approved DONT1/OOS1 and expands risk without being needed for diagnosis.

alternatives_considered.option: Generalize plugin and worker manifests into one framework now
alternatives_considered.rationale: Only two domains exist and worker semantics differ; local duplication remains simpler and lower-risk.

alternatives_considered.option: Capture deployed generation only during plugin initialization
alternatives_considered.rationale: Cannot guarantee AC7's warning on the next transform after a later manifest replacement.

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Proceed after making four points explicit in planning: generate one opaque value before main plugin bundling and inject that exact value; hash final index.js separately and atomically publish schema-v1 manifest; re-read/validate deployed manifest before each system transform and pass typed freshness into the pure assembler; preserve existing runtime-provenance fields while adding separately named bundle freshness fields. Implement deployment as payload rsync excluding plugin-bundle-manifest.json, validate staged payload/manifest, then publish manifest last. Add tests proving build:worker cannot rewrite plugin identity and current/unknown states never emit the stale section.

subagent_reports.recommendation: Accept architecture with caution; require explicit transform-refresh data flow, pre-bundle generation definition, additive health fields, and executable manifest-last deployment sequence before implementation.
follow_ups: TASK_SCOPE, IN_SCOPE, OUT_OF_SCOPE, DONE_WHEN, STOP_WHEN, and VERIFICATION were supplied in the orchestrator packet and followed exactly; no files were edited.
Episode advisory recall returned no relevant project decision; no recalled text was used as evidence.

I do not know whether tsup's onSuccess timing remains stable across every future tsup release; current official docs support async onSuccess after successful JavaScript build, but the simpler project-specific build finalizer should be verified by fixture tests.
Planning should define a bounded unknown-reason enum covering missing, empty, malformed JSON, unsupported schema, invalid generation/hash/timestamp, and unreadable manifest, matching AC4.

decisions.what: Skipped the manifest file existence guard in --dry-run mode.
decisions.why: Dry-run is a preview and may legitimately show a stale dist that would be rebuilt; failing on a missing manifest would break the existing dry-run preview behavior.

decisions.what: Used sha256sum with shasum fallback for index validation.
decisions.why: Keeps the script portable across Linux (sha256sum) and macOS (shasum).

decisions.what: Used jq to extract the expected hash from the manifest.
decisions.why: jq is already a documented dependency for deploy-local --fix config patching, so reusing it avoids adding another tool.

documents.proposal:
## Proposal

1. Stamp a build/generation id into the plugin bundle at build time (mirror the worker `bundle-manifest.json` approach) and capture the loaded stamp at plugin init.
2. On session start / a lightweight probe (e.g. `adv_status` health view), compare the loaded stamp against the on-disk deployed bundle stamp; if the deployed stamp is newer, surface a typed `PLUGIN_BUNDLE_STALE` advisory recommending an OpenCode restart.
3. Optionally emit the advisory in a SESSION_HEALTH-style banner so it is visible without an explicit probe.
4. Document the limitation (no hot-reload) and the restart remedy alongside the existing agent-tool-contracts note.

### Out of scope
- True hot-reload of host-loaded plugin modules (OpenCode platform capability, if ever).

### Acceptance signal
After a build+deploy without restart, a probe reports `PLUGIN_BUNDLE_STALE` with the loaded vs deployed stamps; after restart it reports current.
documents.problemStatement:
## Problem

The ADV plugin is host-loaded by OpenCode at session start (`~/.local/share/Advance/plugin/dist/index.js`). After `pnpm run build` + `deploy-local.sh --fix`, the running session keeps executing the OLD plugin code until OpenCode is restarted. There is no in-session signal that the loaded plugin is stale relative to the deployed bundle — agents silently run old tool behavior.

## Evidence (this session)

- The shipped `fixSubagentPluginToolAccess` durable-evidence matcher + `adv_verification_evidence_disposition` were deployed but NOT live in the running session; the session had to use a free-text-evidence workaround to clear gates because the loaded plugin predated the fix.
- Same failure class as `autoRollStaleWorkerBundle` (worker bundle staleness) but for the PLUGIN bundle. autoRoll solved it for the worker via manifest-generation self-roll; the plugin has no equivalent staleness signal.

## Constraints / nuance

- OpenCode loads plugins at startup; true hot-reload of host-loaded modules may not be possible without an OpenCode-level capability. Scope this as DETECTION + WARNING, not necessarily auto-reload.
- Detection must be cheap and not depend on the (possibly stale) plugin's own newer code.

## Desired outcome

An agent/session gets a clear, early signal when the deployed plugin bundle is newer than the loaded one (e.g. a build/generation stamp mismatch), advising a restart — so stale-plugin friction (silent old behavior, gate wedges) is surfaced instead of discovered the hard way.
documents.agreement:
# Agreement

## Objectives
- Detect when deployed host-loaded plugin code differs from code captured by the running OpenCode session.
- Make mismatch visible early without attempting unsupported hot reload.

## Success Criteria
- SC1: Deployed-versus-loaded plugin identity uses immutable generation equality rather than filesystem timestamps.
- SC2: Confirmed mismatch provides a typed restart remedy without interrupting plugin initialization.
- SC3: Missing or invalid manifest is diagnosable but safe.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC1: A production plugin build writes `dist/plugin-bundle-manifest.json` schema v1 containing a generation, SHA-256 for `index.js`, and ISO `built_at`, with no temporary manifest remaining.
- AC2: A freshly built loaded plugin generation equals its deployed manifest generation and reports `current`.
- AC3: Different loaded and deployed generations report typed `PLUGIN_BUNDLE_STALE`, include both generations, and recommend OpenCode restart.
- AC4: Missing, empty, malformed, unsupported-schema, or unreadable manifest reports bounded `unknown` state without throwing.
- AC5: A deployment that preserves `dist/index.js` mtime but changes manifest generation still reports stale.
- AC6: `adv_status view:"health"` returns loaded generation, deployed generation, freshness state, and recovery action.
- AC7: The next system transform after confirmed manifest replacement emits exactly one `[ADV:PLUGIN_BUNDLE_STALE]` section in the existing system block; current and unknown states emit none.
- AC8: Deployment refuses stale build output when required plugin manifest is missing.
- AC9: Documentation states no hot reload, restart remedy, advisory mtime provenance, and one-restart bootstrap limitation.

## Constraints
- C1: Generation equality is authoritative; timestamp data is diagnostic only.
- C2: Manifest writes are atomic and schema-validated.
- C3: Staleness detection must not crash initialization or mutate runtime code.

## Avoidances
- DONT1: Do not implement plugin hot reload.
- DONT2: Do not use process-start/mtime comparison as stale authority.
- DONT3: Do not overwrite session-health/message-history warning state.

## Out of Scope
- OOS1: OpenCode platform-level module hot reload.
- OOS2: Worker bundle generation behavior.

## Preview Applicability
- visual_surface: false
- preview_expectation: exact_route_required: false; data_state_expectation: none; viewport_expectation: none; rationale: plugin runtime diagnostics only.

## Decisions
### User Decisions
- Confirmed mismatch surfaces typed restart warning and a session-visible banner.
- Invalid deployed manifest reports safe unknown, not false stale.
- Embedded generation plus sidecar manifest determines staleness.

### Agent Decisions (LBP)
- Reuse worker manifest atomic-write pattern, scoped to the plugin build so worker builds cannot overwrite plugin identity.

## Deferred Questions
- None.

## Sign-Off
- User approved criteria and agreement on 2026-07-16.
documents.design:
# Design

## Architecture Overview
Plugin build creates an opaque generation before bundling, embeds it into `index.js`, computes final `index.js` SHA-256 separately, then atomically writes a plugin-specific schema-v1 manifest. Runtime captures embedded generation at evaluation and compares it with a freshly read deployed manifest during each system transform and health probe.

## Key Decisions
- Extend `PluginRuntimeInfo` with loaded/deployed generation, `current|stale|unknown`, bounded unknown reason, and recovery action; retain source/dist mtime provenance additively.
- Stale is typed `PLUGIN_BUNDLE_STALE`; malformed/missing/unreadable manifests safely become `unknown`.
- Add independent stale input/section to existing single system block; never reuse session-health state.
- Deploy excludes manifest from payload rsync, validates copied payload, then publishes manifest last; missing manifest blocks deployment.

## Implementation Strategy
1. Scope pre-bundle generation define and post-bundle manifest writer to plugin production build only.
2. Add parser/comparator with closed unknown reasons and no throws.
3. Capture module-evaluation generation; refresh manifest on every transform/probe.
4. Project additive diagnostics through health status and independent banner.
5. Implement explicit manifest-last deploy sequence.
6. Test equal, mismatch, invalid, mtime-preserved, per-transform refresh, banner, deploy guard, and worker-build isolation.
7. Document restart-only recovery and bootstrap limitation.

## LBP Analysis
Opaque embedded generation answers loaded-versus-deployed identity without self-referential hashing. Per-transform refresh finds later deployment; manifest-last gives one visible publication marker; typed unknown preserves safe host behavior.

## Affected Components
- Plugin build config, plugin manifest/runtime-info/status/system-block/init transform, deployment script, tests, tool-contract documentation.

## Design-Derived Criteria
- DC1: Opaque generation is defined before bundling; final hash remains independent.
- DC2: Loaded generation is never reread from deployed bytes.
- DC3: Every transform/probe rereads only bounded manifest data.
- DC4: Manifest has closed unknown reasons and emits stale banner at most once per transform.
- DC5: Deploy payload copy excludes manifest; validated manifest publication occurs last.

## Design Leverage Scout
- 5 candidates; adopted runtime-info/status seam, bounded unknowns, independent banner, local manifest module, manifest-last publication.

## Validator Result
- Caution, high confidence, medium risk. Resolved: pre-bundle opaque generation, per-transform refresh, additive diagnostics, explicit manifest-last deployment sequence. No contract compromise.

## Risks / Mitigations
- First detector deployment requires one restart; document it.
- Invalid/transient sidecar reports unknown/stale advisory only.
- Plugin and worker build hooks are isolated by tests.
documents.executiveSummary:
# Executive Summary

## Outcome

Advance can now detect — and tell you about — a stale loaded plugin bundle. Every production build stamps an opaque generation into the bundle and writes an atomic sidecar manifest (`dist/plugin-bundle-manifest.json`, schema v1: generation, index.js SHA-256, ISO built_at). At runtime the loaded generation is compared against the deployed manifest.

## Value

The "deployed new code but the session silently runs old code" failure mode — which caused real confusion during this very release cycle — becomes visible and actionable. No more guessing whether a restart is needed.

## Delivered

- Build-time generation stamping + atomic manifest publication (same-directory temp copy + rename; reviewer hardened this so a partial sidecar can never be observed)
- Typed staleness states: `current`, `PLUGIN_BUNDLE_STALE` (both generations + restart recommendation), bounded `unknown` for missing/malformed manifests — never throws, never blocks init
- `adv_status view:"health"` reports loaded/deployed generations, freshness, recovery action
- Exactly one `[ADV:PLUGIN_BUNDLE_STALE]` system-block section after confirmed replacement; none otherwise
- Deploy refuses build output missing the required manifest
- Docs: no hot reload; restart is the remedy; mtime is advisory only; one-restart bootstrap limitation

## Verification

- Independent reviewer verdict: READY, 0 blocking / 0 nonblocking findings
- 295 scoped tests across 9 files green; `pnpm run check` + production build green
- Contract review matrix: 20/20 rows passing/respected/not-applicable
- Generation equality (not mtime) proven authoritative by dedicated mtime-preserving-deployment test

## Risks / follow-ups

- Bundles loaded before this feature existed report `unknown` until one restart (documented bootstrap limitation)
- Deploy fails closed if `jq` or a SHA-256 utility is unavailable on the host
